attrs.evidence: docs/spec/proof-wire/experiment/run_state.mjs resolveState() + containedPath(), enforced from executionProblems() so the transition and the measurement apply it identically; holdout_runner.mjs accepts only --holdout and --summary; holdout_score.mjs accepts nothing; blind_run.mjs refuses --state-root and --repo-root by name. Falsifier P: a REVEALED world with a valid receipt chain cannot authorize a subject one directory outside itself -- the freeze is refused, and the record forced to name it anyway draws a refusal with ZERO H* bytes released. Falsifier Q, the positive dual: a REVEALED world DOES authorize its own subject, so the repair did not cost the dry run. Falsifier J now offers both retired interfaces at once. Gate `gov-nest`; grid boolean authority-bound-to-world, measured on the derivation, the ignored override, and both directions of containment.
attrs.statement: AN AUTHORITY FACT MUST BE BOUND NOT ONLY AS TIGHTLY AS THE FUNCTION CONSUMING IT, BUT TO THE SUBJECT OVER WHICH THAT AUTHORITY IS EXERCISED. P4.7.2 removed the mutable side's ability to SAY "REVEALED" and then left it able to SELECT which state the frozen runner would believe: every lifecycle program took --state-root, so the battery could stop attacking the live record. REPRODUCED: freeze a candidate in the canonical run and never reveal it; copy the record and its receipt chain to /tmp; reveal only the copy; then measure with --state-root pointed at that copy while the repository -- and therefore the candidate executable -- stays canonical. HOLDOUT-AUTHORITY reported PASS over a genuine, internally consistent REVEALED run with a valid chain, and the CANONICAL candidate binary received H1 through H10 while the canonical record still read CANDIDATE_FROZEN. The measurement was stamped NON-CANONICAL, which prevented it from COMPLETING the real run and prevented nothing else: COMPLETION ISOLATION AND SECRET-RELEASE ISOLATION ARE DIFFERENT INVARIANTS, and by the time the stamp applies the irreversible event has happened. The repair is not a special case forbidding one combination; it is removing the ability to form one. The state root is DERIVED as <repoRoot>/governance and repoRoot is derived from the location of the executing program, so a dry run gets a whole WORLD -- its own instrument, release archive, lifecycle programs, record, receipt chain, challenge set and subjects -- rather than a sandbox state directory pointed at the real repository. Every path a run names must be relative and must resolve, symlinks and all, strictly inside its own world. The retired flags REFUSE BY NAME rather than being ignored, because a caller that believes it selected something would otherwise be wrong without being told. THE BOUND: this stops one world's authority reaching another world's subject through the ordinary interface with the record intact; it does not and cannot stop an operator with write access from reading governance/holdout/ directly.
